CheckInIn.description:
Open today's attendance for the calling employee.

There is no `employee_id`: a person punches their *own* attendance, so the record's employee
is the caller's subject reference. A field punch (`work_mode="field"`) at a location that
has a geo-fence must carry a coordinate, and it is checked against the fence server-side.
CheckInIn.title: CheckInIn

CheckOutIn.description: Close today's open attendance for the calling employee.
CheckOutIn.title: CheckOutIn

GeofencePatch.description:
Partial update. Absent means "leave alone"; `location_code` is the org handle a punch is
matched against, so it is not renamed in place.
GeofencePatch.title: GeofencePatch

RegularizationRequestIn.description:
A self-service ask for a correction to your own attendance record (ADR-0006 §11).

There is no `employee_id`, for the same reason `CheckInIn` has none: a person raises a
request against their own record, and the record named in the path already says whose it is.
`reason` is required here — unlike the approver's decision comment, which the platform
deliberately leaves optional (ADR-0006 §7), a request with no stated reason gives an approver
nothing to route on.
RegularizationRequestIn.title: RegularizationRequestIn

RegularizeIn.description:
A direct, audited status correction by an authorised caller. No approval workflow yet
(that is a later slice) — this is the correction itself, recorded with its reason.
RegularizeIn.title: RegularizeIn

ShiftPatch.description:
Partial update. Absent means "leave alone"; `code` is not editable — it is the org handle
other records reference, so a rename is a new shift, not a mutation of the code in place.
ShiftPatch.title: ShiftPatch

info.description: HRMS attendance, shifts and field geo-fencing — part of the OpsGrids platform.
info.title: Attendance service

post.description:
Self-service (ADR-0006 §11). Opens a `pending` request and publishes
`hrms.time.regularization.requested`; approval routes it and reports the decision back on
`core.approval.request.decided`, applied by `app.consumers`.
post.summary: Ask for a correction to your own attendance record

post.description:
The documented escape hatch for a stuck or urgent correction (ADR-0006 §6, §11) — an
administrator changes the status directly, audited in its own domain, unaffected by whether a
self-service request happens to be pending. If one is, its own decision lands later through
the approval consumer and finds the transition it was raised for no longer legal, and reports
`failed` rather than silently overwriting what HR just did.
post.summary: Correct an attendance record's status directly (HR override)

get.description:
How far behind the relay is. **Alert on `oldest_seconds`.**

A stalled relay is the platform's quietest failure. It selects, finds nothing,
logs nothing, sleeps, and loops — `attempts` never increments and `last_error`
stays null, so the process looks healthy indefinitely while the outbox grows
without bound and every consumer downstream starves.

Deliberately **not** part of readiness. A backlog is not a reason to take the
service out of rotation: refusing traffic would stop new events being written
without helping drain the ones already queued, which makes the incident worse.
This is a metric to alert on, not a health state.

Counted through the outbox engine, not the application one. The app role is
NOBYPASSRLS and this request binds no tenant, so through it `pending` would be
zero whatever the table holds — the probe that exists to expose the stall would
be wired to the same blind spot that causes it.
get.summary: Outbox depth and age — scrape this

get.description:
Route traffic on this; restart on /health.

Conflating the two restarts a healthy process that is merely waiting on a
dependency.

Only the dependencies a service actually declares are checked. A gateway owns no
tables, so asking it for a database is asking a question whose answer means nothing
— and a readiness probe that reports on something the service does not use is worse
than no probe, because it will eventually fail for a reason nobody can act on.

Reachable only on the compose `back` network (`tests/infra`'s
`test_metrics_never_routed.py` is the lint that keeps it that way) — never behind
Caddy or a gateway, the same rule `ops_monitor`'s own `/metrics` follows.

`db_pool_in_use` is always reported when this service has a database; the three
outbox gauges only when `outbox_model` is configured — same gate as `/health/outbox`,
and the same reason: an app-role connection with no tenant bound sees zero rows.
